# px0: Read Code. Fast.

> px0 is a fast, lightweight, read-only IDE designed for instant code navigation and review in your browser. Booting in under 1 ms and using ~16 MB of RAM, it turns your browser into a zero-latency inspection console with symbol-level navigation, deep search, and syntax highlighting across massive codebases.

This index is written for large language models and AI agents. It maps the px0 product, its performance characteristics, and its command surface.

## Core resources

- [Home page](https://px0.ai): what px0 is, benchmarks, features, architecture, shortcuts, and installation.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/px0-ai/px0): source, issues, releases, and the install script.
- [README](https://github.com/px0-ai/px0/blob/master/README.md): installation, features, flags, shortcuts.
- [BENCHMARKS.md](https://github.com/px0-ai/px0/blob/master/BENCHMARKS.md): methodology and full results.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/px0-ai/px0/blob/master/ARCHITECTURE.md): internals and performance optimizations.
- [STYLING.md](https://github.com/px0-ai/px0/blob/master/STYLING.md): theme token reference.

## What px0 is

- A single static Go binary (no Electron, no Node, no CGO) that embeds its HTML, CSS, and JS UI.
- Run `px0 [directory]`: it starts a local server on 127.0.0.1:7777, prints the URL, and opens the browser while indexing runs in the background.
- Navigation: fuzzy go-to-file, go-to-symbol, full-workspace regex search, find in file, go to line, back and forward history.
- Optional language servers (gopls, rust-analyzer, typescript-language-server, pyright or ruff, clangd, zls, lua-language-server, solargraph) are detected on `$PATH`, spawned lazily, and fall back to a regex outline when absent.
- 14 built-in themes; Tokyo Night is the default.

## What px0 is not

- Not an editor: it has no write endpoints and does not modify files.
- Not a plugin host: there is no extension marketplace.
- Not a hosted service: it runs locally; the only outbound request is a daily release check against the GitHub API.
